key_idea: Split the downward-closed set by its top bit into S0 and S1+bit with S1 a subset of S0, both downward closed; solve both recursively and glue: x+bit -> f1(x), and y in S0 -> f0(y), plus bit if f0(y) lies in S1.
sketch: Sort the values and recurse on the highest bit of the maximum. The elements with the bit map via f1 onto S1 inside S0; the elements of S0 whose f0-image lies in S1 have that image lifted by the bit (still disjoint since y lacks the bit), which exactly covers S1+bit, and the others keep f0(y), covering S0 minus S1. Base case {0} -> 0. Each level partitions the set, so total work is O(60 n log n) with binary-search membership. Use unsigned 64-bit and 1ULL shifts. Multiple answers are valid, so the sample differs from the checker; samples_passed is true because my own validator (permutation of the input and a_i & b_i == 0) confirmed the sample and 300 random downward-closed sets.
